newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs plan gas plant, eye export link to China.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs plan gas plant, eye export link to China.

text.p: Kazakhstan plans to build a gas condensate refinery on its Karachaganak gas field and may consider constructing a natural gas export pipeline to neighbouring China, senior Kazakh officials said.

"A political decision has been taken with regard to the Karachaganak field -- a refinery with an initial capacity of six million tonnes is being built there," Nurlan Balgimbayev, head of the state Kazakh Oil company, told a news conference on Monday.
He said output at the facility could rise to 15 million tonnes a year.
"There will also be a (natural gas) pipeline to the east, to western China," Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev told a group of Russian media representatives at the weekend.
Balgimbayev said the refinery would be built by the same alliance exploiting Karachaganak -- Agip SpA, British Gas Plc and Texaco.
Agip and British Gas each hold a 32.5 percent stake in the field. Texaco holds 20 percent.
"Probably in May or June, LUKoil will acquire a 15 percent stake owned now by Gazprom, Balgimbayev added, confirming earlier comments by the two Russian energy giants.
Officials have put the cost of tapping Karachaganak on a production-sharing basis at $10 billion over 40 years.
Neither Nazarbayev nor Balgimbayev said when the refinery or pipeline would be built.
Nazarbayev said that processing gas and condensate at refineries in neighbouring Russia was no longer profitable, adding, "why should we incur losses extracting this gas?"
Agip has estimated Karachaganak's proven reserves at 800 billion cubic metres of natural gas and 330 million tonnes of oil and gas condensate.
